bull.b: AP3 gives Acrivon a defined discovery approach centered on matching therapies with patient response signatures. If validated clinically, this precision-oncology capability could improve development focus and support differentiated treatment selection across the company’s pipeline over multiple quarters.

Very low leverage and positive equity provide a stronger financial base than the loss profile alone would suggest. Limited debt can reduce mandatory financing costs and preserve flexibility for clinical development, although the balance sheet remains exposed to continuing operating cash use.

A clinical pipeline of investigational small-molecule oncology candidates provides multiple potential development paths rather than relying on an approved commercial product. Continued trial progress could create future product opportunities and allow the AP3 platform to be applied across more than one candidate.

bear.b: The absence of revenue means Acrivon has not yet demonstrated commercial product demand or operating leverage. The business therefore remains dependent on successful clinical development and eventual approval before recurring sales can support operations, making the investment case fundamentally milestone-driven.

Persistent negative operating and free cash flow shows that development activities consume substantial capital without internally generated funding. Continued burn can reduce financial flexibility over the next several quarters and increase reliance on external financing to maintain clinical programs.

The sharp decline in assets and equity indicates that accumulated losses are steadily reducing the company’s financial resources. Even with low leverage, this erosion can constrain development capacity and leave less balance-sheet support for extended clinical timelines or setbacks.
